pathway: Mitochondrial ribosome assembly and translation
cluster_summary: This cluster shows HIGH confidence for mitochondrial ribosome assembly and translation as the dominant pathway. Approximately 75% of genes (55/73) are established components of the mitochondrial translation machinery, including 39 mitochondrial ribosomal proteins (MRPL/MRPS), aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases (MARS2, YARS2), translation factors (TUFM), and RNA processing factors (PNPT1, MTPAP, LRPPRC, PTCD3, TRMT10C). Additional established genes include mitochondrial protein import components (TIMM50, TIMM17A, TIMM13, TOMM40), mitochondrial quality control factors (YME1L1, OPA1), and respiratory chain assembly factors (COX17, COX18, CHCHD4). The screen's mitochondrial staining (COX4) directly relates to this pathway. Four completely uncharacterized genes (ENSG00000254692, ENSG00000288564, ENSG00000173867, ENSG00000241962) represent high-priority discovery targets as potential novel mitochondrial translation factors. Most striking are several well-characterized genes from other pathways (IRF5, TIA1, FUBP1, TSC1) whose clustering suggests unexpected roles in coordinating mitochondrial translation with immune responses, stress signaling, and growth control.

Additional established genes include mitochondrial protein import components (TIMM50, TIMM17A, TIMM13, TOMM40), mitochondrial quality control factors (YME1L1, OPA1), and respiratory chain assembly factors (COX17, COX18, CHCHD4). The screen's mitochondrial staining (COX4) directly relates to this pathway. Four completely uncharacterized genes (ENSG00000254692, ENSG00000288564, ENSG00000173867, ENSG00000241962) represent high-priority discovery targets as potential novel mitochondrial translation factors. Most striking are several well-characterized genes from other pathways (IRF5, TIA1, FUBP1, TSC1) whose clustering suggests unexpected roles in coordinating mitochondrial translation with immune responses, stress signaling, and growth control.

pathway: Ribosome biogenesis and large ribosomal subunit assembly
cluster_summary: This cluster shows exceptionally high confidence for ribosome biogenesis and large ribosomal subunit (60S) assembly, with >80% of genes directly involved in this pathway. The cluster contains 28 ribosomal proteins (RPL family), multiple ribosome assembly factors (GTPBP4, MDN1, GNL2, RSL24D1, MRTO4), rRNA processing enzymes (NOP2, DDX56, DDX24, DDX54, ISG20L2), and translation initiation factors (EIF4G1, EIF3F, EIF3M). Top discovery priorities include ENSG00000261582 (completely uncharacterized), NOP16 and URB1 (minimal annotation despite nucleolar nomenclature), and novel regulatory roles for CEBPZ (transcription factor), ACTR1A (dynactin component), and RELB (NF-κB factor) in ribosome biogenesis. The morphological phenotypes likely reflect disrupted nucleolar organization, altered ribosome production, or perturbed protein synthesis capacity.

The cluster contains 28 ribosomal proteins (RPL family), multiple ribosome assembly factors (GTPBP4, MDN1, GNL2, RSL24D1, MRTO4), rRNA processing enzymes (NOP2, DDX56, DDX24, DDX54, ISG20L2), and translation initiation factors (EIF4G1, EIF3F, EIF3M). Top discovery priorities include ENSG00000261582 (completely uncharacterized), NOP16 and URB1 (minimal annotation despite nucleolar nomenclature), and novel regulatory roles for CEBPZ (transcription factor), ACTR1A (dynactin component), and RELB (NF-κB factor) in ribosome biogenesis. The morphological phenotypes likely reflect disrupted nucleolar organization, altered ribosome production, or perturbed protein synthesis capacity.

ANAPC2 (APC/C component) and PPRC1 (mitochondrial biogenesis coactivator) suggest novel regulatory connections between cell cycle, metabolism, and ribosome production.

Over 75% of genes are established components: 22 ribosomal proteins (RPS family), 13 SSU processome/pre-rRNA processing factors (UTP, BMS1, PNO1, etc.), 5 translation initiation factors (EIF3 complex), and supporting factors (POLR1B for rRNA transcription, XPO1 for nuclear export, RIOK2 for late maturation). The morphological phenotypes likely reflect disrupted protein synthesis affecting cellular architecture. Key discoveries: Two completely uncharacterized genes (ENSG00000280148, LOC102723573) represent high-priority targets for novel ribosome biogenesis factor identification. HK2 (hexokinase 2) is the most surprising finding - a glycolytic enzyme with no known ribosomal function, suggesting unexpected metabolic coupling to translation machinery. ANAPC2 (APC/C component) and PPRC1 (mitochondrial biogenesis coactivator) suggest novel regulatory connections between cell cycle, metabolism, and ribosome production.

Seven genes with established functions in other pathways show unexpected clustering with replication machinery, suggesting novel roles: CASP8AP2 (beyond histone transcription), ADIRF (adipogenesis factor), CHADL (chondrocyte regulator), CYB5D2 (neuronal differentiation), INSIG1 (cholesterol homeostasis), YLPM1 (telomerase regulation), and AGAP5 (putative GAP). The morphological phenotypes captured by cell painting likely reflect alterations in nuclear organization, chromatin structure, and cell cycle progression resulting from perturbed DNA replication. Histones (H2AC17, H2AC14, H2BC4) and chromatin modifiers (DDB1, KMT5A) support the replication-chromatin assembly connection. The proteasome subunit PSMD3 may reflect quality control of replication factors.
description: Known as negative modulator of chondrocyte differentiation affecting collagen fibrillogenesis. Presence in DNA replication cluster is surprising and may indicate undiscovered role in chromatin organization during replication or cell cycle regulation.

pathway: Pre-mRNA splicing (spliceosome assembly and function)
cluster_summary: Cluster 5 shows HIGH confidence for pre-mRNA splicing as the dominant pathway, with 18/31 genes (58%) being established core spliceosome components representing multiple subcomplexes (U2 snRNP SF3A/SF3B, U4/U6-U5 tri-snRNP, PRP19 complex, LSM proteins). Two completely uncharacterized genes (LOC102724594, ENSG00000289690) represent excellent discovery opportunities as potential novel splicing factors. The most compelling novel roles involve chromatin regulators (MBD6, ZNF335, CXXC1) clustering with splicing machinery, suggesting previously unrecognized coordination between epigenetic state and splice site selection. The morphological phenotypes observed in this OPS screen likely reflect disrupted splicing leading to altered protein isoform expression affecting cellular architecture, particularly given the importance of alternative splicing in cytoskeletal and organellar protein diversity.

cluster_summary: Cluster 7 shows HIGH confidence for translation initiation and termination as the dominant pathway. 16/23 genes (~70%) are established components of translation machinery, including the eIF2 complex (EIF2S1/2/3, EIF2B2/4/5), translation factors (EIF4E, EEF1A1, GSPT1, ETF1), aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases (LARS1, VARS1, SARS1), ribosomal protein RPL12, translation regulator PPP1R15B, and ER chaperone HSPA5 which regulates translation through UPR. PRELID1, PHB2, and SBNO1 are prioritized highest as their clustering with core translation machinery is most unexpected and could reveal novel regulatory mechanisms.

pathway: RNA Polymerase II transcription and elongation
cluster_summary: This cluster shows HIGH confidence for RNA Polymerase II transcription and elongation as the dominant pathway. 17/23 genes (74%) are established components: 10 Pol II core subunits, the general transcription factor GTF2B, the PAF1 complex (PAF1, CTR9, CDC73), the elongation factor SUPT5H, the CTD phosphatase CTDP1, and the CCR4-NOT deadenylation complex scaffold CNOT1. The morphological phenotypes likely reflect altered gene expression patterns affecting cellular organization. Six genes represent high-priority novel role candidates: PLPP4 (lipid phosphatase), RHOC (Rho GTPase), and HMGCR (cholesterol synthesis enzyme) have no established transcriptional roles and would represent surprising discoveries. UBE3A, DDX3X, and SENP6 have some transcriptional functions but their specific clustering with core Pol II machinery suggests more direct mechanistic roles than currently appreciated. No genes are truly uncharacterized - all have substantial literature. The discovery opportunity lies in understanding how metabolic enzymes, cytoskeletal regulators, and post-translational modification enzymes interface with the core transcription machinery.

Core established genes include DNM1L and MFN2 (mitochondrial fission/fusion), RHOT2 (mitochondrial trafficking), SREBF2 (cholesterol biosynthesis transcription factor), SCD and GPAT4 (lipid synthesis), PCYT1A (phospholipid synthesis), SLC25A1 (citrate export for lipogenesis), MARCHF6 (ER-associated degradation of cholesterol enzymes), and VPS13D (lipid transfer at contact sites). The morphological phenotypes likely reflect altered mitochondrial morphology, ER structure, and lipid droplet formation. SMIM12 emerges as the top discovery priority—completely uncharacterized but clustering with well-defined mitochondrial-lipid genes. VHL represents a surprising high-priority candidate, suggesting the hypoxia-sensing E3 ligase may have unrecognized roles in metabolic regulation beyond HIF. SBNO2 and CHP2 offer moderate-priority opportunities to connect transcriptional/calcium signaling to organellar metabolism. Several genes (LSM2, EEF2, CSNK2B) likely reflect indirect housekeeping functions rather than specific pathway roles.
description: Essential translation elongation factor. Presence likely reflects high translation demands of mitochondrial/lipid metabolism genes rather than specific pathway role. Very low priority as function is well-established and connection is indirect.

pathway: Cullin-RING E3 ubiquitin ligase (CRL) pathway
cluster_summary: This cluster shows HIGH confidence for the Cullin-RING E3 ubiquitin ligase (CRL) pathway, with ~75% of genes fitting this process. Core CRL machinery is present (CUL3, RBX1, UBE2M) along with multiple KCTD substrate adaptors (KCTD17, KCTD10, KCTD5). The morphological screen context (actin, membrane, organelle staining) aligns with known CRL functions in cytoskeletal regulation and protein turnover. Top priorities: ENSG00000283321 (completely uncharacterized), BTBD9 (BTB domain protein with no known CRL role), and MUS81 (DNA repair protein with potential novel ubiquitin regulation). Multiple actin regulators (CAPZA2, CAPZB, CFL1) and DNA metabolism proteins (MUS81, POLA2) suggest CRLs coordinate cytoskeletal dynamics with genome maintenance, potentially explaining the morphological phenotypes observed.

Over 75% of genes are established components of this pathway, including integrin heterodimers (ITGAV/ITGB5, ITGB1), focal adhesion kinase (PTK2), adaptor proteins (TLN1, FERMT2, LIMS1, BCAR1), and signaling molecules (ILK, RAC1). The morphological screen detecting changes in actin/plasma membrane staining (AGP) is consistent with focal adhesion disruption. Four completely uncharacterized genes (ENSG00000285238, LOC102723971, LOC124904394, LIMS4) represent top priorities for discovery. LILRA6 and SFPQ are particularly intriguing as established genes from other pathways (immune recognition and nuclear RNA processing, respectively) that may have unexpected roles in focal adhesion biology.
description: Already documented role in BCAR1-CRK-RAPGEF1 signaling for cell adhesion and migration. Connection to focal adhesion pathway is established, not novel.

pathway: Ribosome biogenesis and SSU processome assembly
cluster_summary: This cluster shows HIGH confidence for ribosome biogenesis, specifically SSU processome assembly and pre-18S rRNA processing. 15/20 genes (75%) are established SSU processome components or ribosomal proteins with well-documented roles. The morphological phenotypes likely reflect nucleolar disruption and altered ribosome production affecting cell size, shape, and organelle distribution. LOC102724159 is the top priority as a completely uncharacterized gene clustering with canonical ribosome biogenesis factors. SUPT4H1 represents an intriguing novel connection between transcription elongation machinery and ribosome biogenesis, potentially coordinating rRNA transcription with general transcription. DUSP11's RNA phosphatase activity may play an unrecognized role in pre-rRNA processing. The cluster provides strong validation of the screen's ability to identify functionally coherent gene sets.

pathway: Transcriptional regulation and chromatin remodeling
cluster_summary: This cluster shows high confidence for transcriptional regulation and chromatin remodeling as the dominant pathway. Approximately 79% (15/19) of genes are established components of transcriptional machinery, including: histone modifiers (SETD1B, KAT5, EP400, SPTY2D1), NuA4 complex components (KAT5, EP400, TRRAP), basal transcription factors (GTF2A1, MED10), E2F pathway members (TFDP1, E2F3, TFDP3), RNA processing/termination (INTS6, CNOT3), and ubiquitin-mediated regulation (CUL2, ELOC). Two completely uncharacterized genes (ENSG00000289025, ENSG00000141979) represent high-priority targets for discovering novel transcriptional regulators. ZER1 and ADPRS present interesting cases of established genes in other pathways that may have unrecognized roles in transcriptional control. The morphological phenotypes likely reflect altered gene expression programs affecting cellular architecture through changes in chromatin state and transcriptional output.

Approximately 79% (15/19) of genes are established components of transcriptional machinery, including: histone modifiers (SETD1B, KAT5, EP400, SPTY2D1), NuA4 complex components (KAT5, EP400, TRRAP), basal transcription factors (GTF2A1, MED10), E2F pathway members (TFDP1, E2F3, TFDP3), RNA processing/termination (INTS6, CNOT3), and ubiquitin-mediated regulation (CUL2, ELOC). Two completely uncharacterized genes (ENSG00000289025, ENSG00000141979) represent high-priority targets for discovering novel transcriptional regulators. ZER1 and ADPRS present interesting cases of established genes in other pathways that may have unrecognized roles in transcriptional control. The morphological phenotypes likely reflect altered gene expression programs affecting cellular architecture through changes in chromatin state and transcriptional output.

pathway: Cell cycle regulation and APC/C-mediated ubiquitination
cluster_summary: This cluster shows HIGH confidence for cell cycle regulation, specifically centered on APC/C-mediated ubiquitination and the DREAM/MuvB complex. Six genes are established members: FBXW7 and FZR1 are E3 ubiquitin ligase adaptors, ANAPC10 is an APC/C core component, and LIN9/LIN37/LIN52 form the DREAM complex that regulates G1/S transition genes. The morphological phenotypes likely reflect disrupted cell cycle progression affecting cellular architecture. GARIN5A and CCDC68 are the most promising understudied candidates, with GARIN5A showing particularly interesting potential for a novel cell cycle connection given its limited characterization. Several genes (BTAF1, CDC42BPA, ZNF460) may have novel roles in coordinating transcription or cytoskeletal changes with cell cycle progression, though these connections are less established. The nontargeting control and RPS25 likely represent background noise rather than pathway-specific effects.

Six genes are established members: FBXW7 and FZR1 are E3 ubiquitin ligase adaptors, ANAPC10 is an APC/C core component, and LIN9/LIN37/LIN52 form the DREAM complex that regulates G1/S transition genes. The morphological phenotypes likely reflect disrupted cell cycle progression affecting cellular architecture. GARIN5A and CCDC68 are the most promising understudied candidates, with GARIN5A showing particularly interesting potential for a novel cell cycle connection given its limited characterization. Several genes (BTAF1, CDC42BPA, ZNF460) may have novel roles in coordinating transcription or cytoskeletal changes with cell cycle progression, though these connections are less established. The nontargeting control and RPS25 likely represent background noise rather than pathway-specific effects.

pathway: N-linked glycosylation and dolichol-linked oligosaccharide biosynthesis
cluster_summary: This cluster shows HIGH confidence for N-linked glycosylation and dolichol-linked oligosaccharide biosynthesis pathway (>70% genes directly involved). Eight genes are established pathway members: ALG9, ALG11, and ALG12 are mannosyltransferases adding specific mannose residues to growing oligosaccharides; DHDDS and NUS1 form the DDS complex synthesizing dolichol-PP precursors; DPM2 and GMPPB provide activated sugar donors (dolichol-P-mannose and GDP-mannose); SEC61A1 is the ER translocon for co-translational protein import where N-glycosylation occurs. The morphological phenotypes (particularly ER staining with ConA) align perfectly with disrupted glycosylation. PINLYP is the top priority as a completely uncharacterized gene in this well-defined pathway context. NCEH1 represents an intriguing discovery opportunity as a lipid hydrolase with no known glycosylation role. The remaining genes (KRIT1, TFAP2A, IPO11, EEF1AKMT4) likely have indirect or regulatory connections to the pathway and are lower priorities for pathway-specific follow-up.

pathway: ER-Golgi vesicular transport and SNARE-mediated membrane trafficking
cluster_summary: This cluster shows HIGH confidence for ER-Golgi vesicular transport, with three established SNARE/trafficking genes (SCFD1, GOSR2, STX5) representing ~23% of the cluster. Including plausible supporting genes (CISD3 for organellar coordination, NCALD for calcium regulation), ~38% directly fit the pathway. The morphological screen detecting changes in ER (ConA) and Golgi (AGP) staining strongly supports this pathway. Four highly understudied genes (SAMD10, UBL3, SMIM24, FAM131A) represent excellent discovery opportunities for novel components of the secretory pathway. The core trafficking machinery provides a clear functional framework for prioritizing the uncharacterized genes.

pathway: N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA methylation
